title: Talking Alarm Clocks for Low Vision: What to Check Before You Buy
subtitle: A plain-English guide to clocks that say the time out loud, and the questions worth asking before you order one.
excerpt: A talking alarm clock tells you the time out loud, so you do not have to read a small display. Here is what the listings from one specialty retailer say, and what to confirm before you buy.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: If the numbers on a bedside clock are hard to read, especially in a dim room, a talking clock gives you another way to get the time. Instead of squinting at a display, you press or touch a button and the clock tells you.

Some talking clocks also have alarms and reminders. This guide looks at four listings from MaxiAids, a specialty retailer. It also covers what the listings do not tell us, and what to ask the seller before you order.
The basic idea is simple: press a button, hear the time. The listings below describe it in slightly different ways, so the details are worth a close look.

The Talking Cube Clock is described as having a single large, high-contrast yellow button on top. The Tel-Time Pyramid Talking Alarm Clock is described as giving a time report when you touch its large black top button.

The Large Black Digital Talking Alarm Clock, 7 inches, mentions a button press to hear the time. Its listing keywords also include unlimited alarms and three medicine reminders. The Talking Calendar Alarm Clock is described as having four selectable function controls, with snooze among its features that can be turned on or off. The listings we have do not explain what each of those four controls does, so ask the seller.

One thing to keep in mind: some talking clocks are sold as products "for the blind." That may suit you well if you rely on sound. If you still use some of your sight, you may also want clear, easy-to-read numbers. None of the four listings below was confirmed to describe low-vision use, so ask the seller before you buy.

items: The button. Ask whether there is one large button or several, where it sits, and whether you can find it by touch.
Contrast. If you have some sight, ask how the button and any display look against the clock body.
Display size. If you want to read the time too, ask whether a listed size, such as 7 inches, describes the whole clock or the digits.
Voice and volume. Ask whether the volume can be adjusted, especially if hearing is also a concern.
Alarms and snooze. Count how many alarms you need, and ask whether snooze can be turned on or off.
Power. Ask whether it runs on batteries, plugs in, or both, and whether the time and alarm settings are kept if the power goes out.
Price and returns. The listings we reviewed did not show a price. Confirm the current price, whether the clock is in stock, and the return policy before ordering.

sections.content: Setting it up and using it well
If you are buying for a parent, plan to set the clock up together. Setting the time and alarms may be the trickiest part, so do it with the instructions in front of you and go slowly.
Pick a permanent spot on the nightstand and keep the clock there, so a hand can find it every time. If the clock has a snooze feature, decide together whether it should be on or off.
Keep the instructions somewhere easy to find, and consider writing the key steps in large print. It also helps to test the alarm during the day, so its sound and volume are no surprise at night.

Some listings mention medicine reminders. These are reminders only. They do not hold, sort or dispense pills, and they are not medical devices. Ask the seller exactly how a reminder is delivered. If keeping track of medications is a real concern, see our guide to automatic pill dispensers, and talk with your pharmacist or doctor about the best approach.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: A talking clock will not solve every vision challenge, but it may take one small worry off the nightstand. If your sight is changing, an eye doctor or low-vision specialist can suggest other helpful tools. Start with the questions above, and take your time choosing.
